headline: High: LangGraph’s writable, networked orchestration can amplify unsafe outputs into data leakage and cascading actions when paired with the read-only course repo.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a course repo with no runtime surfaces, while profile B can read/write files, run subprocesses, and use developer-defined tools. A direct injection path is not documented, but if A’s content is manually or file-fed into B, B could misinterpret instructions. The pair lacks a shared channel by default, so this stays low.
conditions: IF A’s repository content is copied into B’s prompt or file input
IF B is configured to treat file contents as instructions
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to all A-derived text
Require explicit human approval before executing tool calls from parsed content

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no egress, but B has broad network egress, filesystem access, and handles model provider API keys. If A and B share a workspace or B reads A-produced files, B can upload those contents to third-party model providers. The interaction is inferred from B’s documented surfaces; A provides no built-in isolation.
conditions: IF A-derived files are placed in B’s readable workspace
IF B forwards workspace contents to model providers or developer tools
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate directories
Block B from reading A’s repo except on demand
Redact secrets before any B tool invocation
Use a local-only model for B when handling A content

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A is non-runnable and has no write or concurrency surface, but B can write the filesystem and uses a shared checkpointer store across instances. If the orchestrator places both on the same mutable workspace, B can overwrite or race on shared files/state. Because A’s runtime behavior is absent, uncertainty does not reduce the risk; the writable default in B makes the conflict dangerous.
conditions: IF B is pointed at the same writable directory as A’s artifacts
IF multiple B instances share the same checkpointer namespace
mitigations: Disable concurrent writers to shared state
Mount A’s artifacts read-only for B

D_cascading_error.rationale: B is an orchestration framework that can chain nodes and developer-defined tools, so A’s outputs can become B’s inputs if wired that way. A itself is a course repo, not a verified runtime, so the main risk is B treating A-derived text as authoritative without validation. That pathway exists in default orchestration patterns, but the blast radius is bounded by the developer’s graph design.
conditions: IF B consumes A-generated text as node input
IF B executes downstream actions without a verification step
mitigations: Insert a validation node before any action-taking step
Require citations or schema checks on A-derived outputs
Log and review all cross-agent handoffs
Mark A outputs as untrusted by default

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source course repo with no touched data classes, while B handles model provider API keys and graph state. No residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented for A, so only a limited compliance gap exists around B’s secret handling and retention of graph state. The other agent is not cited for a specific residency issue because none is documented.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in B’s graph state
IF B’s logs or checkpoints retain secrets beyond policy
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from B checkpoints
Set short retention on graph state
